standard.title: Repetition, rhyme and rhythm
standard.description: explore how repetition, rhyme and rhythm create cohesion in simple poems, chants and songs
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can understand conventions of print and screen including how books and simple digital texts are organised (AC9EFLA04) and have explored rhythms and sound patterns in literary texts at Foundation level (AC9EFLE04). They have not yet explored how repetition, rhyme and rhythm function specifically as cohesion-creating devices within the text as a whole.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore how repetition, rhyme and rhythm create cohesion in simple poems, chants and songs.

nodes.label: Recognising rhyme and repetition
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify rhyming words and repeated patterns in poems, chants and songs.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify rhyming word pairs and a repeated sentence pattern in a given poem or chant.
nodes.typical_width: Identify rhyming words (including end-of-line rhyme), alliterative patterns, and repeated sentence or phrase structures across a range of simple poems, chants and songs.
wider: Identify different types of rhyme (end rhyme, internal rhyme) across a variety of poems
Collect and compare examples of repetition patterns across poems from different cultures or traditions
success_criteria: Student identifies at least one rhyming pair in a given text
Student identifies a repeated phrase or sentence pattern in a poem or chant

nodes.label: Repetition and rhyme hold the text together
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how repetition and rhyme create a sense of pattern and predictability that holds a poem, chant or song together.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how a repeated pattern in a given poem or chant helps the reader or listener know what comes next.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss how repetition and rhyme create cohesion — a sense of wholeness and connection — in poems, chants and songs, using specific examples from familiar texts.
wider: Compare two versions of a poem — one with repetition removed — and discuss how cohesion changes
Explore how chants and songs use repetition functionally to aid memory and communal participation

response_modes.reason: The concept of cohesion is abstract for Year 1 students. Multiple text examples — poems, chants, songs — where students can feel the 'pull' of repetition and rhyme help make the abstract idea concrete and transferable.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparing texts with and without repetition, or exploring communal functions of chant repetition, gives advancing students genuine insight into how structural devices shape a reader's or listener's experience — rich literary and linguistic territory.
success_criteria: Student explains, with reference to a specific example, how a repeated pattern helps the text feel connected
Student identifies at least one way repetition or rhyme signals to the reader or listener what comes next

nodes.label: Rhythm creates pattern in sound
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify rhythm in a poem or chant and describe how it contributes to the text's pattern and flow.
nodes.minimum_width: Clap or mark the beat of a familiar poem or chant and describe the rhythmic pattern.
nodes.typical_width: Identify rhythm in poems, chants and songs by marking beats, describe the rhythmic pattern, and discuss how rhythm contributes to the text's flow and cohesion alongside rhyme and repetition.
wider: Compare fast and slow rhythms across poems and discuss how rhythm affects mood
Explore rhythm in First Nations Australian songs or chants and discuss how rhythm serves cultural and communal purposes

response_modes.reason: Rhythm, rhyme and repetition are three distinct devices that work together — this node requires students to see how rhythm joins the other devices to create overall cohesion, not just identify another isolated feature.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations Australian songs and chants offer a culturally significant context for exploring how rhythm functions beyond aesthetic pleasure — in cultural transmission, ceremony and communal memory.
success_criteria: Student can mark or demonstrate the beat pattern of a given poem or chant
Student describes how rhythm combines with rhyme or repetition to give the text its pattern
